name: DeepFluoro (DeepFluoroLabeling-IPCAI2020)
aka: Grupp et al. JHU cadaveric hip fluoroscopy; JHU Data Archive doi:10.7281/T1/IFSXNV
anatomy: pelvis, proximal femur and lower lumbar vertebrae (cadaver)
size: 6 cadaveric lower-torso specimens, 366 registered C-arm frames (Siemens CIOS Fusion), one CT per specimen; full-resolution HDF5 2.5 GB
annotation_detail: 2-D and 3-D segmentations of six structures (left/right hemipelvis, vertebrae as one class, upper sacrum, left/right femur), 14 bilateral pelvic landmarks, per-frame ground-truth pose
how_to_get: Follow the JHU Data Archive DOIs in the GitHub README (full-resolution HDF5 doi:10.7281/T1/IFSXNV/EAN9GH, 2x-16x downsampled versions also listed; original CT and fluoroscopy files doi:10.7281/T1/C304HZ); the archive sits behind Cloudflare, so use a browser or a browser-fingerprinted client such as curl_cffi.
paper: Grupp RB et al., Automatic annotation of hip anatomy in fluoroscopy for robust and efficient 2D/3D registration, IJCARS 2020; arXiv:1911.07042
notes: The reference real C-arm set with per-frame pose and CT, but vertebrae are a single unnamed class and the field is pelvis-centred, so it serves calibration and DRR fidelity rather than level naming.

name: C-ArmLSpine
aka: Zhang et al., FIRST Surgio-B51 intraoperative lumbar C-arm set (Zenodo 22768651)
size: 149 cases, each with AP and lateral intraoperative frames and a CBCT from the same C-arm; Greg's copy counts 299 spot frames, 602 sweep projections and 149 CBCTs; 15.6 GB zip
annotation_detail: No labels ship; Greg's copy adds TotalSegmentator/SPINEPS level names on each CBCT and frame poses by 2-D/3-D registration
how_to_get: Download C-ArmLSpine.zip (15.6 GB, md5 6bccd47979a2a1c9b200dc427fefeb54) from Zenodo record 22768651.
paper: Zhang et al., Medical Image Analysis 97:103283 (2024), doi:10.1016/j.media.2024.103283 (cited by the record)
notes: The closest public match to the target task (living patients, intraoperative lumbar AP and lateral frames with a same-session CBCT), limited to one C-arm model and needing level labels transferred from the CBCT.

name: COBRA2026
aka: COBRA: Cone-Beam CT Reconstruction for Radiation Therapy challenge (grand-challenge, MIDL 2027)
anatomy: pelvis of radiotherapy patients, with lower lumbar spine and sacrum in the field
size: 867 pelvic cases from six European centres (692 training, 52 validation, 123 test), about 950 GB; each case a full raw kV CBCT projection sweep
annotation_detail: Per-projection RTK geometry.xml, metadata.yaml with kV/mA/filter settings, projections simulated from a deformably registered planning CT, clinical and RTK CBCT reconstructions, field-of-view masks
how_to_get: Zenodo 21322350 holds the overview zip and dataset paper; the ~750 GB training set is hosted externally and fetched with the download script from the organisers' preprocessing repository; validation and test are embargoed (release listed as 2032-03-01); the challenge needs a grand-challenge.org account.
paper: Thummerer A, Rit S, Kamp F, Maspero M et al., COBRA2026: a large-scale multicenter pelvic cone-beam computed tomography projection dataset, arXiv:2607.20037
notes: Linac-mounted kV imagers (Elekta, Varian) rather than mobile C-arms, but the only large real-projection set with exact geometry and a registered CT for checking DRR physics frame by frame.

name: 2D-3D-GS lumbar spine gold standard
aka: Ljubljana 2D-3D-GS; Tomaževič, Likar, Pernuš (LIT, University of Ljubljana)
size: CT, MR and 18 turntable X-ray images of one cadaveric L1-L5 specimen; 75 MB zip
annotation_detail: Fiducial-based gold-standard registrations for each vertebra between CT, MR and X-ray images, with evaluation software and a user guide
how_to_get: Download 2D-3D-GS.zip and the user guide 2D-3D-GS.pdf from the LIT resources page; the user guide asks users to sign the lab's agreement form, so read it before use.
paper: Tomaževič D, Likar B, Pernuš F, gold standard for 2D/3D registration of the lumbar spine, MICCAI 2002 (citation in the user guide)
notes: One donor imaged on a flat panel rather than a C-arm, but every vertebra carries its own gold-standard pose, which suits testing per-level registration.

name: Geneva hip 2D-3D registration gold standard
aka: D'Isidoro et al. 2021, University of Geneva Yareta archive
size: One female hip phantom: 116 fluoroscopic frames over 19 views (Philips BV Pulsera image intensifier) plus CT; 481 files, 394 MB
annotation_detail: Gold-standard rigid transforms and calibrated projection matrices with uncertainty modelling
how_to_get: Download the archive from Yareta (doi:10.26037/yareta:2kw5s2jadbbv3ngtkzsovihtnu); the record also lists a contract on the use of data.
license: CC BY-SA 4.0 on the record (the paper text says CC BY-NC 4.0)
paper: D'Isidoro F et al., 2D-3D registration gold-standard dataset for the hip joint based on uncertainty modeling, Medical Physics 2021, doi:10.1002/mp.15124
notes: A phantom, but it adds an image-intensifier C-arm with exact geometry, useful for fitting a second device's image-formation model.

name: SpineSAC
aka: IGRS lab, HTIC / IIT Madras phantom C-arm 2D/3D registration set
size: 59 AP plus lateral acquisition scenarios on three sawbone phantoms across several C-arms, each with a CT; Greg's copy 5,492 files, 4.15 GB
annotation_detail: Projection matrices for the AP and lateral views, initial and ground-truth 6-DoF poses, vertebra ROI boxes per view; no level names
how_to_get: Download each subfolder of the Google Drive folder linked in the README, keeping the folder names so the dataset paths resolve.
license: No data licence stated (README badge MIT, code section Apache-2.0)
paper: No paper listed in the repository
notes: Several C-arms with poses make it useful for device variation, though sawbones lack soft tissue and reuse terms are unstated.

name: xvr-data
aka: eigenvivek/xvr-data on Hugging Face (DeepFluoro, femur and Ljubljana repackaged for xvr/PolyPose)
size: 32 rows, 4.84 GB
annotation_detail: DICOM/NIfTI versions of three registration datasets; the card does not list per-file contents
how_to_get: huggingface-cli download eigenvivek/xvr-data --repo-type dataset (authenticate to avoid HTTP 429).
license: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 overall; DeepFluoro part CC BY-NC 4.0
paper: The card asks users to cite the original DeepFluoro, femur and Ljubljana papers
notes: Greg holds only its deepfluoro/ subfolder; the femur and Ljubljana parts are convenient DICOM/NIfTI copies of sets listed separately here.

name: SX-Stitch intraoperative scoliosis C-arm images
aka: Li et al. 2024, SUSTech and Peking Union Medical College Hospital
anatomy: thoracolumbar spine with pedicle screws (scoliosis surgery)
size: 1,032 intraoperative C-arm images at 512, 1024 and 1920 px; consecutive frames of one patient overlap by 20-90%
annotation_detail: Pedicle-screw segmentation masks used for stitching; how they were annotated is not described
how_to_get: The paper has no data statement or link; write to the corresponding authors (Greg's draft docs/data_requests/SX-Stitch_request.md in spinesurg-ct-nnunet has not been sent).
paper: Li Y, Gao H, He M, Liang J, Gu J, Liu W, SX-Stitch: an efficient VMS-UNet based framework for intraoperative scoliosis X-ray image stitching, arXiv:2409.05681
notes: The nearest thing to real intraoperative thoracolumbar C-arm sequences with hardware, but nothing is released and the C-arm make is not stated.

name: Balgrist ex-vivo lumbar CT and fluoroscopy set
aka: Jecklin et al., X23D domain-adaptation data (Balgrist University Hospital, Zurich)
anatomy: lumbar spine L1-L5 (13 ex-vivo specimens plus 6 validation specimens)
size: 1,017 paired synthetic-real X-ray images (4,337 vertebra crops) on a Siemens Cios Spin; validation specimens also on Ziehm Vision and Ziehm Vision FD
annotation_detail: CT vertebra segmentations projected to 2-D masks, 14-fiducial calibration with checked 2-D positions, DRRs rendered from the same poses
how_to_get: The data availability statement offers code only on request (pending patent) and points to CTSpine1K for the synthetic base; write to the corresponding author (Greg's draft docs/outreach/balgrist_data_request_2026-09-21.md offers a DUA through Wayne State).
paper: Jecklin S et al., Domain adaptation strategies for 3D reconstruction of the lumbar spine using real fluoroscopy data, Medical Image Analysis 2024; arXiv:2401.16027
notes: Three C-arm models with fiducial poses and CT on lumbar specimens would directly test device transfer, but the authors restrict it.

name: Bone-substructure-contour multi-view X-ray/CT dataset
aka: Flepp et al., Balgrist and University Children's Hospital Zurich (Zenodo 15753063)
size: 5 specimens, 10 calibrated C-arm views each (Siemens, Fluorospot Compact S1, 976x976 px), one CT per specimen; 6.7 GB zip
annotation_detail: Per-view pose from a removable 16-bead fiducial (inlier reprojection error below 0.8 px), contour labels of diaphysis and condyles, matching CT
how_to_get: Download dataset_ipcai.zip from Zenodo record 15753063.
license: Research-Only Dataset License (commercial use needs written permission)
paper: Flepp R et al., Automatic multi-view X-ray/CT registration using bone substructure contours, IJCARS 2025, doi:10.1007/s11548-025-03391-4; arXiv:2506.13292
notes: Another real C-arm with exact poses and CT, useful for image-formation fitting though not spine.

name: Veriserum
aka: ETH Zurich Laboratory for Movement Biomechanics dual-plane knee fluoroscopy dataset
anatomy: knee implant phantoms (femoral and tibial TKA components)
size: About 110,000 dual-plane images (1664x1600 px) from 1,600 robot-driven trials of 10 implant pairings
annotation_detail: Automatically registered ground-truth pose for every image, manual poses for a benchmark subset (200 in the paper, 390 in the README), distortion and source-intensifier calibration
how_to_get: Download the images, calibrations and sqlite pose database from ETH Research Collection doi:10.3929/ethz-b-000701146; loader code is at github.com/wjh19990923/Veriserum.
license: In Copyright - Non-Commercial Use Permitted (README); described as free for academic and research use
paper: Veriserum: a dual-plane fluoroscopic dataset with knee implant phantoms for deep learning in medical imaging, MICCAI 2025; arXiv:2509.05483
notes: Large and pose-exact, but a custom bi-planar image-intensifier rig imaging metal implants, so it helps pose-regression methods rather than spine appearance.

name: CAMS-Knee
aka: Comprehensive Assessment of the Musculoskeletal System, knee (ETH Zurich and Charité, OrthoLoad)
size: 6 subjects, repeated cycles of 5 daily activities; moving-fluoroscope sequences synchronised with implant loads, gait, EMG and video
annotation_detail: 3-D tibio-femoral implant kinematics from moving fluoroscopy, implant forces and moments, marker kinematics, ground reaction forces, 16-channel EMG
how_to_get: Use the Data Request page on cams-knee.orthoload.com; a sample download and live demo are on the same site.
license: Not stated on the portal home page (research use on request)
paper: Taylor WR et al., A comprehensive assessment of the musculoskeletal system: the CAMS-Knee data set, Journal of Biomechanics 2017, doi:10.1016/j.jbiomech.2017.09.022
notes: The portal does not say whether raw fluoroscopy frames ship, and it is knee only.

name: XMAPortal (X-ray Motion Analysis Portal)
aka: XROMM data portal, Brown University; new portal xma.xromm.brown.edu
size: Many studies; size varies by study
annotation_detail: Per study: raw biplane X-ray videos, calibration images, CT, metadata and processed tracking files
how_to_get: Open All Studies and pick a Public Study to view and download its videos without logging in; the legacy site is read-only and new work is on xma.xromm.brown.edu, where accounts are requested through Documentation.
license: Set per study by its owner
paper: No single dataset paper (portal of many XROMM studies)
notes: A rare source of raw high-rate biplane fluoroscopy with calibration, but almost entirely non-human and non-clinical.

name: Cervical Spine Kinematics Database from Fluoroscopic Imaging
aka: Bournemouth quantitative fluoroscopy, BORDaR 385 (Branney, Breen, Breen)
anatomy: cervical spine (neck-pain patients and matched controls)
size: Greg's harness notes: 63 subjects, 126 imaging events x flexion/extension = 252 sequences at 15 Hz; one 24 MB MAT file, no pixels
annotation_detail: Vertebral body positions in Cartesian coordinates from template-tracked four-corner vertebrae (C0-T1 per Greg's harness notes), with intervertebral angles, translation and disc height; the source 1024x1024 16-bit images are not included
how_to_get: Download Cervical Database.mat and the README files from the BORDaR record.
paper: Branney J, Breen A, Breen A, Cervical Spine Kinematics Database from Fluoroscopic Imaging, Bournemouth University 2024, doi:10.18746/bmth.data.00000385; companion article J Funct Morphol Kinesiol 2024;9(1):55, doi:10.3390/jfmk9010055
notes: Corner tracks only (the DICOM cine is not public), so it can check motion priors but cannot train an image model.

name: 3D-2D-GS-CA cerebral angiogram registration gold standard
aka: Ljubljana 3D-2D-GS-CA (Mitrović, Špiclin)
size: 10 patients (aneurysm, AVM) with 3D-DSA, 2D-DSA and 2D-MAX images; ten zips of 85-120 MB plus a gold-standard zip
annotation_detail: Fiducial-marker gold-standard 3D-2D registrations with projection geometry
how_to_get: Download the user guide, the ten dataset zips and the gold-standard zip from the LIT resources page.
paper: Mitrović U, Špiclin Ž, Likar B, Pernuš F, 3D-2D registration of cerebral angiograms: a method and evaluation on clinical images, IEEE TMI 2013, doi:10.1109/TMI.2013.2259844
notes: Real clinical C-arm frames with exact geometry from living patients, though cranial and angiographic rather than spinal.

name: ARCADE
aka: Automatic Region-based Coronary Artery Disease diagnostics using X-ray angiography imagEs (MICCAI 2023 challenge)
size: Two tasks of 1,200 images each (1,000 train, 200 validation) plus two 300-image test sets; 452 MB
annotation_detail: SYNTAX-segment vessel polygons (26 classes) and stenosis boxes in COCO-style JSON
how_to_get: Download arcade.zip from Zenodo record 10390295 (earlier version: record 8386059).
paper: Popov M et al., Dataset for automatic region-based coronary artery disease diagnostics using X-ray angiography images, Scientific Data 2024, doi:10.1038/s41597-023-02871-z
notes: Clean, permissively licensed cine-derived frames that can teach fluoroscopic texture and noise, with no skeletal labels.

name: CADICA
aka: Coronary artery disease invasive coronary angiography dataset (Málaga)
size: 668 invasive coronary angiography videos from 42 patients, 1-151 frames each at 512x512 and 10 fps (over 6,000 frames)
annotation_detail: Lesion bounding boxes on keyframes, lesion and non-lesion video lists, per-video ground-truth tables, a projections JSON and clinical metadata
how_to_get: Download version 5 from Mendeley Data (doi:10.17632/p9bpx9ctcv.5); a Kaggle copy is ariadnapartinen/cadica-a-new-dataset-for-coronary-artery-disease.
paper: Jiménez-Partinen A et al., CADICA: a new dataset for coronary artery disease detection by using invasive coronary angiography, Expert Systems 2024;41(12):e13708; arXiv:2402.00570
notes: Whole cine sequences rather than single frames, useful for temporal fluoroscopy models but with no skeletal content.

name: XCAD
aka: X-ray coronary angiography dataset of the SSVS paper (Ma et al.)
size: Unlabelled training angiograms and background images, plus a test split with vessel masks (126 test angiograms per later papers); 512x512
annotation_detail: Radiologist vessel masks for the test split only; the training split is unlabelled for self-supervised learning
how_to_get: Download XCAD.zip from the Dropbox or Baidu NetDisk (key neia) link in the SSVS README.
paper: Ma Y et al., Self-supervised vessel segmentation via adversarial learning, ICCV 2021, doi:10.1109/ICCV48922.2021.00744
notes: Small labelled split and no licence; at most a source of cardiac fluoroscopy texture.

name: DCA1 (Database of X-ray Coronary Angiograms)
aka: CIMAT / IMSS León coronary angiogram database
size: 130 angiograms per the page (archive named DB_Angiograms_134.zip), 300x300 grayscale PGM
annotation_detail: Expert cardiologist vessel ground truth per image
how_to_get: Download DB_Angiograms_134.zip from the CIMAT page and cite the paper.
paper: Cervantes-Sanchez F et al., Automatic segmentation of coronary arteries in X-ray angiograms using multiscale analysis and artificial neural networks, Applied Sciences 2019;9(24):5507, doi:10.3390/app9245507
notes: Small, low-resolution and vessel-only, so little value beyond texture.

name: Angiographic dataset for stenosis detection
aka: Danilov et al., Kemerovo coronary stenosis set (Mendeley ydrm75xywg)
anatomy: coronary arteries (100 patients with one-vessel disease)
size: 8,325 grayscale frames (512x512 to 1000x1000) from 100 patients
annotation_detail: Stenosis bounding boxes drawn in LabelBox on frames showing contrast through the stenotic vessel
how_to_get: Download version 2 from Mendeley Data (doi:10.17632/ydrm75xywg.2).
paper: Danilov VV et al., Real-time coronary artery stenosis detection based on modern neural networks, Scientific Reports 2021, doi:10.1038/s41598-021-87174-2
notes: Two vendors' systems (Siemens Coroscop, GE Innova) in one open set, handy for vendor-appearance variation in fluoroscopy.

name: DIAS
aka: DSA-sequence Intracranial Artery Segmentation dataset
size: DSA sequences from intracranial interventions (120 in the arXiv paper; a later paper cites 60); 292 MB zip
annotation_detail: Pixel-wise artery masks plus two kinds of scribble labels for weakly supervised segmentation
how_to_get: Download DIAS.zip from Zenodo record 11637181 (linked from github.com/lseventeen/DIAS).
paper: Liu W et al., DIAS: a dataset and benchmark for intracranial artery segmentation in DSA sequences, Medical Image Analysis 2024, doi:10.1016/j.media.2024.103247; arXiv:2306.12153
notes: Subtraction removes bone, so it says little about spine appearance.

name: CathAction
aka: AIRVLab endovascular catheterisation benchmark
anatomy: endovascular procedures in silicone phantoms and animals
size: About 500,000 annotated frames and 25,000 catheter/guidewire masks (paper v1); 56.2 GB on Hugging Face
annotation_detail: Action labels (advance or retract catheter or guidewire, rotate), collision boxes, catheter and guidewire segmentation masks
how_to_get: Fill in the Google Form on the download page and accept the licence; the files are on huggingface.co/datasets/airvlab/CathAction.
paper: Huang B, Vo T et al., CathAction: a benchmark for endovascular intervention understanding, arXiv:2408.13126
notes: A large volume of real fluoroscopy video, but vascular phantom and animal scenes with no skeletal labels.

name: Guide3D
aka: AIRVLab bi-planar guidewire dataset
size: 8,746 bi-planar frames at about 1024x1024 (6,136 Radifocus, 2,610 Nitrex); 4.07 GB
annotation_detail: Manual guidewire polylines and segmentation masks in two views for 3-D shape reconstruction
how_to_get: huggingface-cli download airvlab/guide3d --repo-type dataset; code at github.com/airvlab/guide3d.
paper: Jianu T et al., Guide3D: a bi-planar X-ray dataset for guidewire segmentation and 3D reconstruction, ACCV 2024; arXiv:2410.22224
notes: Bi-planar phantom fluoroscopy of instruments only, marginal for spine.

name: DysphagiaBank UNM Dysphagia Corpus
aka: TalkBank DysphagiaBank; Palmer, University of New Mexico swallow studies
anatomy: oropharynx and cervical spine in lateral and AP view (videofluoroscopic swallow studies)
size: 7 participants listed on the corpus page; Greg's copy is 19 GB of video
annotation_detail: CHAT transcripts of each videofluorographic swallow evaluation (bolus and events); no image annotations
how_to_get: Transcripts download as a zip from the corpus page; the media folder on media.talkbank.org asks for a TalkBank login.
license: TalkBank rules: cite Palmer et al. 2023 (Greg's manifest records CC BY-NC-SA and a no-LLM-use condition)
paper: Palmer PM, Padilla AH, MacWhinney B, The development and implementation of a data repository for swallow studies, Dysphagia 2023;39:476-483, doi:10.1007/s00455-023-10632-8
notes: Lateral cine of living cervical spines at fluoroscopic dose, but with no vertebra labels and a no-LLM condition that Greg recorded.

name: VFSS2022
aka: Video-TransUNet VFSS data (Bristol)
size: 440 frames per the TIB listing
annotation_detail: Bolus and pharynx/larynx instance masks
how_to_get: None: the repository says ethics approval covers use and display in the paper only, not release.
paper: Zeng C et al., Video-TransUNet: temporally blended vision transformer for CT VFSS instance segmentation, ICMV 2022; arXiv:2208.08315
notes: Indexed as a dataset by TIB but the images are not released, so it is a dead end.

name: VCUG VUR Dataset (Kaggle)
aka: saidulkabir/vcug-vur-dataset
anatomy: bladder, ureters and kidneys (paediatric voiding cystourethrography)
size: 113 PNG images in Grade 1-5 folders, 12 MB
annotation_detail: Vesicoureteral reflux grade per image (folder name)
how_to_get: kaggle datasets download -d saidulkabir/vcug-vur-dataset (Kaggle account required).
paper: No dataset paper; used in arXiv:2506.11508
notes: Images were collected from public sources, so quality and reuse rights are uncertain, and there is no spine value.

name: HSG data (Mendeley)
aka: Hysterosalpingography images, Gansu Provincial Maternity and Child Health Hospital
size: 892 images
annotation_detail: Four tubal-patency classes (bilateral patency, bilateral blockage, unilateral patency, bilateral partial patency) labelled by three radiologists
how_to_get: Download from Mendeley Data (doi:10.17632/9pjjb3j58p.1).
paper: No paper listed on the record (Mendeley Data, January 2026)
notes: Pelvic contrast fluoroscopy of soft-tissue structures, of no direct use for vertebral labelling.

name: PENGWIN Task 2 synthetic X-ray
aka: PENGWIN 2024 (MICCAI) pelvic fragment segmentation on synthetic X-ray; Hugging Face mirror MedOtter/PENGWIN_Task2
anatomy: pelvis: sacrum and both hip bones with fracture fragments
size: 50,000 DeepDRR renders from 100 CTs (500 per CT), half with up to 10 simulated K-wires or screws; train.zip 35 GB
annotation_detail: Overlapping multi-label uint32 masks for sacrum, left and right hip fragments (bits 1-10, 11-20, 21-30)
how_to_get: Download train.zip and pengwin_utils.py from Zenodo record 10913196; the validation and test X-rays were never released.
license: CC BY 4.0 (Zenodo); the Hugging Face mirror applies CC BY-NC-SA 4.0
paper: Benchmark of segmentation techniques for pelvic fracture in CT and X-ray: summary of the PENGWIN 2024 challenge, arXiv:2504.02382 (IEEE TMI 2026); rendering per doi:10.1007/978-3-031-43996-4_30
notes: Greg holds the PENGWIN 2026 CTs but not these renders, which give unwindowed C-arm-geometry DRRs with surgical hardware and sacrum masks for hardware-robustness training.

name: FluoroSeg
aka: Training set of FluoroSAM (Killeen et al., JHU ARCADE lab)
anatomy: whole body (head and neck, torso, lower extremity)
size: 2,953,257 DRRs from 1,621 CTs (2,814,214 train, 139,043 validation); 2.65 TB
annotation_detail: Image, mask and text triplets for organs and computer-modelled surgical tools
how_to_get: Log in to Hugging Face, accept the conditions on benjamindkilleen/fluoroseg (contact information is shared), then download; reader code is at github.com/arcadelab/fluoroseg.
paper: Killeen BD et al., FluoroSAM: a language-promptable foundation model for flexible X-ray image segmentation, MICCAI 2025; arXiv:2403.08059
notes: The largest released CT-to-fluoroscopy corpus, but whether vertebrae are named by level and whether per-image geometry ships is not yet documented.

name: SyntheX benchmark data
aka: Data for 'Synthetic data accelerates the development of generalizable learning-based algorithms for X-ray image analysis' (JHU Data Archive)
anatomy: hip and pelvis (plus surgical-tool and COVID chest subsets)
size: hip_imaging.zip 2.07 GB, surgical_tool_detection.zip 5.0 GB, covid.zip 1.6 GB
annotation_detail: Training and test files for the hip landmark and segmentation benchmark built from NMDID CT simulations and matched against real cadaver C-arm images (Siemens CIOS Fusion, Brainlab Loop-X)
how_to_get: Download hip_imaging.zip from the JHU Data Archive (doi:10.7281/T1/2PGJQU); Cloudflare blocks scripted clients, so use a browser or curl_cffi; usage is documented in github.com/arcadelab/SyntheX.
paper: Gao C, Killeen BD et al., SyntheX, Nature Machine Intelligence 2023;5:294-308, doi:10.1038/s42256-023-00629-1; arXiv:2206.06127
notes: The standard sim-to-real C-arm benchmark, useful for comparing Greg's render physics against a published domain-randomised pipeline on the same real frames.

name: VinDr-SpineXR
aka: VinDr-SpineXR 1.0.0 (PhysioNet)
size: 10,466 images from 5,000 studies (8,389 train, 2,077 test); Greg's copy 48 GB
annotation_detail: Radiologist boxes for 13 lesion types plus 'no finding'; no vertebra levels
how_to_get: Create a PhysioNet account, complete credentialing, sign the PhysioNet Restricted Health Data Use Agreement 1.5.0, then download.
paper: Nguyen HT et al., VinDr-SpineXR: a deep learning framework for spinal lesions detection and classification from radiographs, MICCAI 2021, arXiv:2106.12930; data doi:10.13026/q45h-5h59
notes: Native DICOM films with no level labels; a Kaggle upload (siddhale937e92739/annotated-medical-image-dataset-for-spinal-lesions) re-hosts it under MIT, which the DUA does not allow, so that copy should not be used.

name: BUU-LSPINE
aka: Burapha University lumbar spine dataset (400 sample, 3600 full release)
anatomy: lumbar spine and sacrum, AP and lateral
size: Full release 3,600 patients, 7,200 films (AP and left lateral); public 400-patient sample
annotation_detail: Upper and lower end-plate edge points per lumbar vertebra (CSV) and physician diagnoses of antero-, retro- and laterolisthesis
how_to_get: Download the 400-pair sample from the Google Drive link on the BUU page; for the full set submit the Google Form (name, affiliation, purpose) and accept the EULA, and approved requests are sent by email.
license: EULA (no re-identification, acknowledgement required, no endorsement); no open licence
paper: Klinwichit P et al., Applied Sciences 2023;13(15):8646, doi:10.3390/app13158646
notes: The largest lumbar film set with end-plate geometry, but level names follow row order and Greg found four- and six-lumbar cases in it.

name: NHANES II cervical and lumbar spine X-ray images
aka: NCHS NHANES II (1976-1980) spine films, formerly hosted by NLM
size: 17,075 films (9,667 cervical, 7,408 lumbar) from 9,700 participants
annotation_detail: No readings or annotations are released
how_to_get: Follow 'Cervical and Lumbar Spine X-ray Images (August 2025)' on the NHANES II page to the CDC FTP server and download individually or by script.
paper: NCHS NHANES II X-ray documentation (no dataset paper)
notes: Digitised 1970s films (12-bit scaled to 16-bit TIFF) with no labels; their value is volume for pseudo-labelling.

name: NHANES II Spinal X-ray with Extra Labels for Reference Vertebral Bodies (C2, S1)
aka: Mo, Papiez, Chen, Mandal, Jabbar (Zenodo 10223910); VertXNet labels
size: About 600 annotated films in one 1.0 GB zip (Greg's copy: 543 pickles)
annotation_detail: Vertebra coordinates from the original NLM annotation plus radiologist reference points for C2 and S1; Greg's copy holds per-level masks keyed C2-C7, T1, T11-T12, L1-L5, S1
how_to_get: Download NHANESII_Annotations_VertebralOsetophytes.zip from Zenodo record 10223910.
paper: Mo Y et al. (VertXNet), Scientific Reports 2023, doi:10.1038/s41598-023-49923-3
notes: One of the few film sets where each vertebra is named and anchored to C2 and S1, which matches the level-naming task.

name: AASCE 2019 / SpineWeb Dataset 16
aka: BoostNet AP scoliosis films (London Health Sciences Centre, EOS)
size: 609 labelled AP films (481 train, 128 test) plus 98 unlabelled challenge test films
annotation_detail: 68 landmarks per film (four corners of 17 vertebrae, T1-L5) and three Cobb angles; corrected corner files on Zenodo 4413665
how_to_get: Request through the SpineWeb datasets page (its host did not resolve on 2026-10-17); corrected annotations only are on Zenodo record 4413665.
paper: Wu H et al., Automatic landmark estimation for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis assessment using BoostNet, MICCAI 2017, doi:10.1007/978-3-319-66182-7_15; Wang L et al., Medical Image Analysis 2021, doi:10.1016/j.media.2021.102115
notes: Seventeen vertebrae in a fixed order imply T1-L5 names, but the curated release documents swapped and shifted labels, so the order cannot be trusted blindly.

name: Cervical Spine X-ray Atlas (CSXA)
aka: CSXA V3.0, Dongzhimen Hospital, Beijing University of Chinese Medicine
size: 4,963 PNG films with 4,963 JSON annotation files
annotation_detail: 23 keypoints per film: four corners of each of C3-C7 and three points on the C2 lower end plate; curvature class, 118 quantitative parameters, pixel scale
how_to_get: Download the images from Science Data Bank (doi:10.57760/sciencedb.15391; Greg's notes say it needs a browser session) and the spreadsheet and code from the GitHub repository.
license: CC BY 4.0 for the article (Greg's manifest records CC BY 4.0 for the data); repository code GPL-3.0
paper: Ran Y et al., A high-quality dataset featuring classified and annotated cervical spine X-ray atlas, Scientific Data 2024;11:625, doi:10.1038/s41597-024-03383-0
notes: Level-named cervical corners on nearly 5,000 films make it the best open cervical training set, though it stops at C7.

name: Spinal-AI2024
aka: CurvNet data-engine scoliosis films
size: 20,000 generated images in 5 subsets of 4,000; 2.7 GB
annotation_detail: COCO-format vertebra annotations and three Cobb angles per image
how_to_get: Clone the GitHub repository or download its subset and annotation zips.
paper: Chen et al., CurvNet: latent contour representation and iterative data engine for curvature angle estimation, Pattern Recognition; arXiv:2411.12604
notes: Generated by a data engine rather than acquired, so it adds shape variety but no real acquisition physics.

name: Lateral Full-spine X-ray Image Dataset
aka: IEEE DataPort, Yitong Pan (236 films)
size: 236 JPG films (about 3000x7000 px), 910 MB zip
annotation_detail: No annotations in the release
how_to_get: Log in to IEEE DataPort with a subscription and download the zip.
paper: Pan Y, Lateral full-spine X-ray image dataset, IEEE DataPort 2021, doi:10.21227/pacw-ws92
notes: Full-length lateral films let levels be counted from C2, so they can supply count-derived level labels, but nothing is annotated.

name: Spondylolisthesis Vertebral Landmark
aka: Mendeley Data 5jdfdgp762 (Honduran set plus BUU-LSPINE subset)
size: 716 images (208 Honduran, 508 from BUU-LSPINE); 698 annotated
annotation_detail: Vertebral boxes and four corner keypoints per vertebra from L3 to S1, in Keypoint R-CNN JSON
how_to_get: Download from Mendeley Data (doi:10.17632/5jdfdgp762.1).
paper: No paper citation given on the record
notes: Includes S1 corners on spondylolisthesis cases but overlaps BUU-LSPINE for 508 images, so it must be deduplicated against BUU.

name: TVGH-SpineXR
aka: IEEE DataPort doi:10.21227/x6bb-7r75
anatomy: thoracolumbar spine, lateral (per Greg's 2026-09-22 probe record)
size: Not known
annotation_detail: Greg's probe noted T1-L5 level labels, masks and end plates from the record text; nothing was confirmed here
how_to_get: Log in to IEEE DataPort and open the DOI; anonymous access returns 'Access denied', and whether a subscription is needed was not confirmed.
paper: IEEE DataPort record doi:10.21227/x6bb-7r75 (no paper found)
notes: Possibly a second level-labelled thoracolumbar film set, but its page refuses anonymous access and none of its details could be checked.

name: LUMOS
aka: Lumbar Multimodal Osteoporosis Screening dataset (Zhejiang University)
size: 803 patients: 1,620 lumbar radiographs (AP or lateral) and 280 lumbar CTs; 46.4 GB
annotation_detail: Osteoporosis class from T-scores and DXA BMD, BMC, T- and Z-scores for L1-L4; no image annotations
how_to_get: Download the CT zips (lumos_ct_*) and X-ray zips (lumos_x_*) from Zenodo record 18173664; rename lumos_x_741_670_dcm.zip to lumos_x_741_770_dcm.zip as the record notes.
paper: Shi K et al., LUMOS: a lumbar multimodal osteoporosis screening dataset with X-ray and CT images, ACM MM 2025, pp. 13250-13257, doi:10.1145/3746027.3758282
notes: Real lumbar DR films in DICOM alongside lumbar CTs from the same cohort, the only open set where a DRR-versus-real comparison on living lumbar spines may be possible, though the film-to-CT pairing is not documented.

name: A dataset of scoliosis, spondylolisthesis, and normal vertebrae X-ray images
aka: Fraiwan, Audat, Manasreh (King Abdullah University Hospital, Jordan); Kaggle mirror yasserhessein/the-vertebrae-xray-images
size: 338 subjects (188 scoliosis, 79 spondylolisthesis, 71 normal); 91 MB on the Kaggle mirror
annotation_detail: Diagnosis class per subject
how_to_get: Download from Mendeley Data (doi:10.17632/xkt857dsxk.1).
paper: No paper listed on the record (Mendeley Data, January 2022)
notes: Class labels only at small scale; it adds one more hospital's film appearance.

name: VertebraeKeypoints50
aka: Kaggle c3ls1y/vertebraekeypoints50
anatomy: whole spine and lumbar spine, lateral
size: About 50 PNG films by its name (80% full-length, 20% lumbar) and one XLSX table; 132 MB
annotation_detail: Anterior and posterior end-plate points for every named vertebra C2-S1 (Th12-S1 on lumbar films)
how_to_get: kaggle datasets download -d c3ls1y/vertebraekeypoints50 (Kaggle account required).
license: Open Database License for the database, Database Contents License for the contents (as declared)
paper: None
notes: Tiny and of unstated origin, but one of very few open lateral full-spine sets with every vertebra named from C2 to S1.

name: Scoliosis YOLOv5 Annotated Spine X-ray Dataset
aka: Kaggle salmankey/scoliosis-yolov5-annotated-spine-x-ray-dataset (several near-duplicate versions by the same uploader)
size: 252 MB with train, validation and test splits
annotation_detail: YOLO boxes for 'Vertebra', 'scoliosis spine' and 'normal spine'
how_to_get: kaggle datasets download -d salmankey/scoliosis-yolov5-annotated-spine-x-ray-dataset (Kaggle account required).
license: MIT as declared by the uploader
paper: None
notes: Typical of Kaggle spine sets: origin not stated, boxes without level names, and several near-duplicate versions.
